intro.alt: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions - report evidence

intro.text: Kalinga University, Raipur, is committed to promoting peaceful, inclusive and just societies by strengthening institutional accountability, transparency, ethical governance and respect for human rights. The University actively contributes to SDG 16 through its Faculty of Law, Legal Aid Cell, Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), Anti-Ragging Committee, Grievance Redressal Cell and various student welfare initiatives. These institutional mechanisms ensure access to justice, protect individual rights, promote gender equality and provide a safe, inclusive and discrimination-free campus environment.

The University conducts legal awareness programmes, workshops, seminars, awareness campaigns and community outreach activities to educate students and local communities about constitutional values, fundamental rights, legal responsibilities and social justice. Through NSS, the Department of Students' Welfare (DSW) and student-led initiatives, the University encourages civic responsibility, peaceful coexistence, democratic participation and ethical leadership.

Furthermore, Kalinga University promotes transparent administrative practices, responsible decision-making and effective grievance redressal mechanisms to ensure institutional integrity and accountability. By integrating legal education, community engagement and good governance practices, the University strives to develop socially responsible citizens and contribute towards building peaceful, inclusive and sustainable communities in alignment with United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 16.

blocks.text: Kalinga University promotes research on peace, justice, human rights, constitutional values, social inclusion and good governance through its Faculty of Law and interdisciplinary research initiatives. Faculty members and scholars undertake research addressing legal reforms, gender justice, access to justice, human rights protection, conflict resolution and social equity. Through research publications, seminars, conferences and community engagement, the University contributes to strengthening legal awareness, promoting peaceful coexistence and supporting transparent, accountable and inclusive institutions in alignment with SDG 16.
16.1.1 Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions: Citescore

Kalinga University actively contributes to SDG 16 through research focusing on peace, justice, human rights, good governance and strong institutions. The University has published 41 cumulative research papers, receiving a total of 76 citations, reflecting the research impact and scholarly contributions in this area. These publications promote legal awareness, social justice, institutional accountability, transparency and inclusive development, supporting the University's commitment to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 16.
16.1.2 Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions: FWCI

University demonstrates its research contribution to SDG 16 through 41 publications addressing peace, justice, human rights, good governance and institutional accountability. These publications have achieved a Field-Weighted Citation Impact (FWCI) of 0.85, indicating their citation performance relative to the global average in corresponding research fields. This research contributes to advancing legal awareness, social equity, transparency and inclusive institutional development.
16.1.3 Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions: Publications

Kalinga University has demonstrated consistent growth in research publications aligned with SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions. As illustrated in the graph, the University recorded no aligned publications in 2021 and 2022, followed by 7 papers in 2023 and 4 papers in 2024. A significant increase was observed in 2025, with 22 research publications, representing the highest annual contribution. In 2026, the University recorded 9 publications. These research contributions reflect growing academic engagement in areas such as human rights, social justice, legal reforms, good governance, institutional accountability and peaceful societies.

16.2.1 Elected Representation 2025

Kalinga University has implemented a Policy for Students' Council to promote student participation, leadership development, representation, communication and responsible engagement in institutional activities. The Council provides a structured platform for students to express suggestions and concerns and actively participate in academic, cultural, sports, technical, social, sustainability, community-service and student-welfare initiatives.

The Council is constituted through election, nomination, selection or a combination of these methods, as approved by the competent authority, ensuring appropriate student representation. Representatives must fulfil prescribed eligibility criteria, including satisfactory academic performance, attendance, discipline and conduct.

The Council facilitates teamwork, peer engagement and constructive communication between students and university authorities. Periodic meetings are conducted, with proper records of agendas, attendance, minutes, suggestions and action-taken reports. Student welfare concerns are communicated to appropriate authorities, while formal grievances are referred to designated grievance redressal mechanisms and statutory committees.
A Faculty Advisor or Student Council Coordinator guides and monitors its functioning. All activities require prior university approval and follow prescribed financial procedures.

Through this initiative, Kalinga University promotes student empowerment, democratic participation, transparency, accountability and responsible leadership, contributing to SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

blocks.text: 16.2.2 Students’ Union 2025

Kalinga University does not have a formal Students' Union; however, it has an officially approved Students' Council Policy to promote student representation, leadership and participatory governance. The Council facilitates student engagement in academic, cultural, sports, technical, social and community-service activities. It communicates student suggestions and welfare concerns to university authorities. Guided by a Faculty Advisor/Coordinator, the Council promotes inclusivity, discipline, transparency, accountability and responsible leadership, contributing to SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.
16.2.3 Identify and Engage With Local Stakeholders 2025

Kalinga University is committed to promoting sustainable development, inclusive economic growth, community engagement and meaningful partnerships through its Policy for Identification and Engagement with Local Stakeholders. The policy provides a structured framework for identifying, connecting and collaborating with relevant local stakeholders to strengthen institutional and community relationships.

The University engages with diverse stakeholders, including local communities, government bodies, industries, employers, NGOs, civil society organisations, alumni, local entrepreneurs, farmers and community-based organisations. These collaborations aim to create mutually beneficial opportunities for knowledge sharing, skill development, internships, employment, entrepreneurship, research and community development.

Through its various academic departments, schools, Placement and Training Cell, Alumni Cell, Extension and Outreach units, and IQAC, the University facilitates stakeholder consultations, collaborative activities, capacity-building programmes and community outreach initiatives. These engagements provide students with practical exposure, industry-oriented skills and opportunities for professional development while addressing local and regional needs.

The Deans, Heads of Departments, faculty members and concerned administrative units are responsible for stakeholder mapping, consultation, engagement, documentation and periodic review to ensure effective implementation of the policy.

Through this systematic approach, Kalinga University strengthens university–community partnerships, promotes employability and entrepreneurship, supports local economic development and contributes to achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through inclusive and sustainable stakeholder engagement.

blocks.text: 16.2.4 Participatory Bodies for Stakeholder Engagement 2025

Kalinga University promotes active stakeholder participation through various institutional bodies, departments and outreach units to strengthen university–community relationships and encourage inclusive development. The National Service Scheme (NSS) Unit, Department of Students' Welfare (DSW), Young Indians (YI), Alumni Cell, Placement and Training Cell, IQAC and academic departments across all eight Schools actively engage students, faculty members, local communities and external stakeholders.

These participatory bodies organise awareness programmes, workshops, seminars, skill-development activities, community outreach initiatives and collaborative events focusing on social responsibility, digital literacy, civic awareness, employability, entrepreneurship, environmental sustainability and community welfare. They also facilitate interaction with government organisations, industries, NGOs, alumni and local community groups to address regional needs and promote mutually beneficial partnerships.

During the academic year 2025, several initiatives were undertaken to encourage stakeholder involvement, strengthen community participation and provide students with opportunities for experiential learning, leadership development and social engagement. These activities reflect the University's commitment to participatory governance and sustainable development.

blocks.text: 16.2.5 University Principles on Corruption and Bribery 2025

Kalinga University upholds a zero-tolerance approach towards corruption, bribery, fraud and unethical practices. The University's Code of Conduct is applicable to the Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Chief Finance Officer (CFO), Controller of Examinations (COE), all teaching and non-teaching employees, and students. It emphasises honesty, integrity, transparency, accountability and fairness in all academic, administrative and financial activities. All members are expected to avoid bribery, conflicts of interest, undue influence, favouritism and misuse of institutional authority or resources. The University promotes ethical decision-making, responsible governance and compliance with applicable laws, policies and institutional regulations to ensure a fair, transparent and accountable environment, in alignment with SDG 16.

blocks.text: 16.2.6 Academic Freedom Policy

Kalinga University promotes academic freedom as an essential foundation of quality education, research excellence and intellectual independence. The University's Academic Freedom Policy encourages faculty members, researchers and students to engage in independent teaching, learning, research, critical thinking, academic discussions, debates and knowledge sharing while maintaining ethical and professional standards. The University supports intellectual exploration through conferences, seminars, workshops, research programmes and publication opportunities. This policy fosters innovation, knowledge creation, responsible academic participation and institutional development, contributing to SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

blocks.text: 16.2.7 Publish Financial Data

Kalinga University promotes financial transparency, accountability and responsible resource management through the preparation and maintenance of audited financial statements, balance sheets and income-expenditure reports. Regular statutory audits ensure financial accuracy, regulatory compliance and appropriate utilisation of institutional resources. Relevant financial information is shared with stakeholders through appropriate institutional channels, including the official website, wherever applicable. These practices strengthen ethical financial management, institutional integrity and good governance, contributing to SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

blocks.text: Kalinga University actively collaborates with various government departments, ministries, statutory bodies and public institutions to promote education, research, innovation and sustainable development. The University participates in and organises government-supported initiatives, programmes, workshops, seminars, training sessions, awareness campaigns and community outreach activities. Through these collaborations, the University contributes to skill development, environmental sustainability, social welfare, digital literacy, entrepreneurship and public awareness. Faculty members and students actively engage in government-led initiatives, strengthening institutional partnerships and community participation. These collaborative efforts support regional development, public welfare and the achievement of SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.
16.3.1 Provide Expert Advice to Government

Kalinga University actively contributes to SDG 16.3.1 through collaboration with government departments and local authorities by conducting community-oriented extension activities, awareness campaigns, health initiatives, blood donation drives, surveys and environmental programmes, including tree plantation. Through NSS, Young Indians (YI), DSW and various academic departments, the University engages students and faculty in public welfare initiatives. These partnerships promote civic responsibility, social justice, community well-being and sustainable development while strengthening University–Government collaboration and institutional engagement.
16.3.2 Policy- and Lawmakers Outreach and Education

Kalinga University promotes meaningful engagement with policymakers, legislators, government officials and public institutions through its Policy on Engagement, Outreach and Education for Policymakers and Legislators. The University facilitates knowledge exchange through research dissemination, policy dialogues, seminars, conferences, workshops, expert interactions and capacity-building programmes. These initiatives encourage evidence-based decision-making, public awareness and informed understanding of governance and societal issues. All engagements follow a non-partisan, academically responsible approach, focusing on education, research, knowledge sharing and sustainable development.

blocks.text: 16.3.3 Participation in Government Research

Kalinga University encourages faculty members and researchers to actively participate in government-funded research projects and initiatives supported by various national and state-level agencies, including DST, AICTE, ICSSR, DBT, CSIR, BIRAC, CGCOST, NABARD, Chhattisgarh Tourism Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board (CECB), Watershed Development Component (WDC), Chhattisgarh Regional Science Centre, Unnat Bharat Abhiyan, NITI Aayog and other public funding organisations.

Through its Research and Development Cell, the University promotes research collaboration, innovation, knowledge creation and interdisciplinary studies addressing national and societal challenges. It facilitates research proposals, funding applications, grant management, financial documentation and compliance with relevant funding guidelines. These collaborations strengthen academia–government partnerships, encourage evidence-based research and contribute to national development, technological advancement, environmental sustainability and SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.

blocks.text: 16.3.4 Neutral Platform to Discuss Issues

Kalinga University provides an inclusive and neutral platform for constructive discussions on social, legal, academic and policy-related issues. Through seminars, conferences, panel discussions, workshops and awareness programmes, the University encourages meaningful interaction among students, faculty members, government representatives, industry experts and civil society organisations. These activities promote open dialogue on peace, justice, governance, gender equality, human rights and sustainable development. The University encourages evidence-based discussions, mutual respect, diverse perspectives and informed decision-making, strengthening institutional transparency, social responsibility and SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.
